## The idea

A transcription error becomes expensive when pitch, rhythm, and expression are
all uncertain at once. I first tried to capture a melody note by note in one
pass. Every correction shifted the later events, so I could no longer tell
whether a wrong entrance came from the source, my hearing, or an earlier edit.

The four-pass pipeline keeps one class of uncertainty in view at a time. Pass 1
records tempo, meter, and phrase boundaries. Pass 2 records rhythm without
pitch. Pass 3 adds contour and a few anchor pitches. Pass 4 settles exact
pitches, articulation, dynamics, and timing detail. Each pass produces data
that the next pass can inspect.

Do not skip forward because one note seems easy. A confident isolated pitch can
hide a bar that is half a beat short. Mark uncertainty in the data with a
searchable comment such as REVIEW. That marker is a work queue, not an
admission of failure.

## Run this

The example renders the same four-beat phrase after each pass. Integer notes
stand in for MIDI pitches because pitch arithmetic is the point here.

```{.ruby audio=""}
use_bpm 76
use_synth :beep

rhythm = [0.5, 0.5, 1, 0.5, 0.5, 1]
contour = [0, 1, 2, 4, 2, 0]
tonic = 60
exact_notes = [60, 62, 64, 67, 64, 60]

define :play_pass do |notes, durations, amp|
  notes.zip(durations).each do |pitch, duration|
    play pitch, release: duration * 0.75, amp: amp
    sleep duration
  end
end

# Pass 2: one repeated pitch exposes rhythm without melodic distraction.
play_pass [tonic] * rhythm.length, rhythm, 0.6
sleep 1

# Pass 3: contour uses relative steps from a provisional anchor.
play_pass contour.map { |step| tonic + step }, rhythm, 0.8
sleep 1

# Pass 4: the exact spelling replaces the provisional contour.
play_pass exact_notes, rhythm, 1.0
```

The first version sounds like a rhythm exercise. The second acquires a shape.
The third changes two whole-tone guesses into exact pitches, while the duration
sum remains four beats.

## Change one thing

1. Change the last rhythm value from 1 to 0.5. All three renderings now end
   early. Listen to how clearly a shared rhythmic fault survives later pitch
   work.
2. Change the fourth contour step from 4 to 3 without changing exact_notes. The
   middle rendering reaches a lower high point, while the final pass stays
   fixed. This is the gap between a contour hypothesis and a settled pitch.
3. Add the comment REVIEW beside one exact note, then search the buffer for
   REVIEW. Use the log or editor search as a queue for unresolved events.

## Why it works

Each pass is an interface with a narrow contract. The rhythm pass must account
for the meter, but it does not need to name a pitch. The contour pass must
preserve that rhythm and describe direction. Exact pitch entry can then compare
candidate notes against known anchors without reopening the duration problem.

Pass 1 often lives as comments or metadata rather than playable events. Write
the meter, estimated tempo, pickup length, and phrase boundaries first. A
phrase boundary is especially useful because it limits the damage from a wrong
duration. You can validate four bars independently instead of allowing one
missing eighth note to offset the rest of the piece.

The event schema remains stable across passes. A reusable event eventually has
:note, :start, and :duration, with optional :amp. During rhythm entry, :note can
hold a neutral placeholder. During contour entry, it can hold a provisional
value. The final pass replaces it. Stable keys make diffs readable and allow
the same validation helpers to run throughout the work.

This resembles a compiler pipeline. An early stage establishes structure,
later stages enrich the representation, and diagnostics stay attached to the
smallest useful unit. Skipped structure returns as ambiguous debugging.

## Take it further

Choose eight bars from one candidate in your source inventory. Create a
transcription checklist with four signed-off passes and a fixed event schema.
After each pass, save a separate version or commit. The target is an eight-bar
event array whose durations validate before exact pitch entry begins. Leave
every uncertain event marked REVIEW, and include a short note explaining what
evidence would resolve it.
